assumptions: Severity is the key's own reading. missing_term, value_out_of_range and duplicate_card are blocking; printed_value_mismatch, note_conflict and denominator_unexpected are warnings. docs/SPEC.md 5.1 names the kinds but not the severities.
A duplicated school year blocks every subject until the approver chooses a card.
A score recorded out of another denominator is converted to the template's scale (score x scale / denominator) and raises a denominator_unexpected warning.

The window is the last window_terms term scores that exist for the subject (or, for a skill, the last window_terms terms in which every subject of the area has a score). Fewer than min_scores means not_enough_evidence.

The level is the stage-weighted average of the window (CA-4). The gap is the distance from the level to the nearest edge of the range for the stage of the last term (CA-5). The gap direction compares the first term's gap (against its own stage's range) with the last term's gap, using the TR-4 threshold.
A change of exactly the threshold is not a move (TR-2 says 'more than').
